calls.title: SDK Design Improvements Kickoff
calls.summary: The team met to streamline the SDK page by merging connection details and improving clarity on connection status, as led by Guy Langford-lee and Kari Kay. The plan includes moving connection information to the page header for better visibility and collapsing settings based on connection status to enhance user experience. Johnny Martinez was guided on updating UI components through a phased approach, focusing first on outdated modals and main page elements. The discussion also emphasized the need for clear revision selectors and the combination of connection and revision statuses within the UI. Additionally, layout optimization was proposed to reduce wasted space and enhance metadata display, with Kari ensuring ongoing collaboration with Johnny for efficient onboarding.
calls.keywords: SDK design, connection status, approval flow, modal rebuild, UI components, copyable snippets

calls.title: SDK Design Improvements Kickoff
calls.summary: The team discussed strategies to simplify the SDK connection setup flow, including hiding advanced settings initially to lower cognitive load and speed up setup time. They emphasized the importance of clearer descriptions for payload security options, advocating for concise tooltips instead of lengthy tutorials. The need for better documentation links was identified to avoid clutter and enhance clarity during setup instructions. Additionally, breaking the large SDK connection modal into smaller panels was proposed for easier editing and improved user satisfaction. Visibility of connection scope details, such as environment and project information, was deemed essential for better user understanding, while plans for segregating webhook management settings and integrating approval workflows were also outlined.
calls.keywords: SDK connections, payload security, remote evaluation, UI redesign, documentation, webhook approvals

calls.title: SDK Design Improvements Kickoff
calls.summary: The team discussed enhancing the SDK connection user experience by simplifying the connection page, particularly by hiding advanced settings that are rarely used. Guy Langford-lee highlighted the need to break the setup process into clear steps to reduce confusion, especially regarding payload security options. The group agreed to revise the existing instructions to link to internal documentation rather than external sources. Additionally, the design improvements included breaking the large connection modal into smaller, manageable sections to reduce cognitive load and clearly displaying connection statuses for better user awareness. Furthermore, webhooks will be organized into a dedicated tab to streamline the user interface. Finally, the team outlined next steps, including rebuilding modals with updated components for consistency.
calls.keywords: SDK connection, payload security, remote evaluation, modal redesign, approval flow, webhook settings
